lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is weddings. And I have big news: last Saturday I went to my first Azerbaijani wedding!
My cousin's wedding! Tell everyone how many guests there were.
Five hundred! In England, a big wedding is maybe a hundred people.
[laugh] Five hundred is normal here. Cousins, neighbours, colleagues, neighbours of colleagues…
And the dancing! Four hours of dancing. My legs hurt more than after a long run.
What did you think of the bride and groom?
They looked so happy. But the ceremony was short — the party was the main event.
That's a tradition here. The official part is often a few days before, just with the family.
And someone gave a toast every ten minutes!
Did you give one?
I did! In Azerbaijani. Three sentences. Everyone clapped — I think because they were surprised.
[chuckle] They loved it. But you know who can always steal the show?
Aysu! She danced with the groom's grandfather!
For twenty minutes! Now, what about weddings in England?
My sister just got engaged. She and her boyfriend want a small wedding — forty guests, in a garden.
Forty! My mum would say that is just the family. When will they tie the knot?
Next summer. And I'm going to give the toast — in English this time. [laugh]
Will you bring the Azerbaijani dancing to England?
Definitely. Forty English people dancing for four hours — they won't know what hit them.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: what is a typical wedding like in your country — big or small?
And what's the best wedding you've ever been to? See you next time!
Bye for now!
